intro: Occupational therapy assistants already coach patients through daily tasks with patience and care. The closest of the 25 careers below is Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses, with an 88% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $64,400, which is 11% less than the $72,300 these assistants earn.
why_it_works: Each session you follow a care plan, adapt activities and notice small signs of progress or pain. O*NET rates social perceptiveness and service orientation at 3.88 out of 5 for this job. Nursing, respiratory therapy and adapted physical education use the same patient focus. Only some matches pay more, and most of those need more schooling. The skills to grow are coordinating care and clinical judgment.
tips: If you want more pay, compare bridge programs to occupational therapist degrees; the job earns $100,330, or 39% more.
Respiratory Therapists earn $82,280, which is 14% more, after an associate-level program.
Keep notes on the patients and conditions you have worked with; clinics hire for specific experience.

faq.q: What jobs can former occupational therapy assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are licensed practical nurses (88%), Acute Care Nurses (81%) and Respiratory Therapists (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. Registered Nurses are also 79% matched and earn $97,550, which is 35% more than the $72,300 assistant median, though they need a nursing degree.

faq.q: Which careers for occupational therapy assistants pay more?
faq.a: 6 of the 25 matches pay more. Radiation Therapists earn $105,310 (46% more), Physical Therapists $102,760 (42% more) and Occupational Therapists $100,330 (39% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. The two therapist roles usually need a graduate degree, while radiation therapy needs a specific program.

faq.q: Do occupational therapy assistants need more education to switch?
faq.a: Usually yes for a raise. Only 8 of the 25 matches need no more education than assistants already have, and 2 need a graduate degree. In a close nursing match, 57% of workers hold a bachelor's degree, so plan for some extra study.

faq.q: What skills should occupational therapy assistants build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are coordination, instructing, judgment and decision making and complex problem solving. Time management already rates 3.5 out of 5 for your job in O*NET, so clinical decision making is the main step toward nursing or therapist roles.
